title: Expected Minimum Degree of Common Transistor Parity Checks
summary: The prior degree estimate does not extend naively to full Transistor because of a subfield relation; the expected minimum degree of a common parity check at each weight remains unknown.

formal_statement.body: Determine, for each prescribed polynomial weight, the expected minimum degree of a parity-check polynomial for full Transistor that is valid simultaneously for the key LFSR and the whitening LFSR, equivalently a multiple of $\operatorname{lcm}(P_{\mathcal K},P_{\mathcal W})$, where $P_{\mathcal K}$ and $P_{\mathcal W}$ are their feedback polynomials. The estimate must account for $P_{\mathcal W}$ defining a subfield of the field defined by $P_{\mathcal K}$ and therefore cannot be obtained merely by replacing $|\mathcal K|$ with $|\mathcal K|+|\mathcal W|$ in the prior degree estimate.

scope.domain: Linear cryptanalysis of full Transistor using parity-check polynomials common to its key and whitening LFSRs.
assumptions: The whitening feedback polynomial defines a subfield of the field defined by the key feedback polynomial.
parameters: Prescribed polynomial weight: fixes the target weight of the parity-check polynomial
Polynomial degree: the quantity whose expected minimum is sought
Key and whitening feedback polynomials P_K and P_W: their least common multiple determines the required common-multiple condition
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the expected minimum degree at each prescribed weight while accounting for the subfield relation instead of applying the prior estimate with the key and whitening sizes added.

progress.summary: The paper notes that an attack on full Transistor requires a parity-check polynomial valid for both LFSRs and that their subfield relation prevents extending the earlier estimate by simply adding the register sizes. It leaves the corresponding expected minimum-degree estimate open.
citation_labels: Jules Baudrin et al., Transistor: a TFHE-friendly Stream Cipher
